subject: SageWorks hosted API — data wipe, residency & retention details
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@sageworks.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@sageworks.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up — residency / retention + deletion SLA for hosted API

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal flagged a couple of items in the questionnaire around data residency and deletion timelines for the hosted API: specifically (1) where customer data is physically stored by default (we're US-only), (2) how long request payloads / model outputs are retained, and (3) what the SLA is for a tenant-initiated deletion request (including backups and cached artifacts).

Can you send a concise set of answers we can paste into the questionnaire? Also, if you have a short matrix or diagram mapping what lives in what storage tier (logs, ephemeral KV, backups), that would be great to attach.

Best,
Jordan
VP Product, SageWorks
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@sageworks.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — residency / retention + deletion SLA for hosted API

Jordan —

Appreciate the follow-up. I attached a compact response workbook (scc_answers_sageworks.xlsx) and a one-page residency matrix (redwood_data_residency_matrix.pdf). Below are the answers formatted for the questionnaire; feel free to copy/paste. If Legal wants any rewording, flag it and we’ll iterate.

1) Data residency (hosted API):
- Default storage region: US (primary: us-west-2). We also offer explicit region pinning (us-east-1, eu-west-1) at the account level for customers on an enterprise plan. For SageWorks (per our intake) we will enforce US-only storage for all persisted artifacts.

2) Data categories & storage mapping:
- Request payloads and generated outputs (customer content): persisted in encrypted object storage (S3) in the pinned region for up to 30 days by default.
- Inference runtime caches (KV/prefix caches): held in-memory on GPUs and in short-lived SSD-backed caches; these are non-persistent and recycled per-instance; when an instance is terminated or scaled down, the in-memory cache is discarded. For safety, we do not treat KV caches as durable storage.
- Aggregated telemetry/usage logs: anonymized metrics aggregated and stored for 365 days for product telemetry. Request-level debug logs (trace-level): retained 30 days and then permanently deleted.
- Backups & snapshots: nightly snapshots of the inference environment (for recovery) are stored encrypted and retained for 14 days by default in the same region.

3) Deletion / Erasure process (hosted API):
- Tenant-initiated deletion (account data purge): Redwoodsupports a programmatic erase endpoint for hosted accounts. For SageWorks we will escalate to our priority deletion workflow. The SLA for a full logical account purge across primary storage and request-level logs is 72 hours from request acknowledgment. Backups/snapshots are garbage-collected within 30 days of the purge request to ensure forensic recoverability windows are respected.
- Runtime caches and ephemeral KV: purged immediately (within minutes) as part of the purge workflow; we also proactively rotate/recreate serving instances to ensure no cached artifacts are reused.
- Audit trail: Once purge completes we provide an exportable audit record with timestamps and the affected object IDs.

4) Proofs & evidence:
- We can provide redacted sample audit exports, a runbook of the erase workflow, and an on-demand live audit during onboarding if Legal requires.

5) Encryption & access controls:
- Data at rest: AES-256. Data in transit: TLS1.2+. Customer-managed KMS available for enterprise tenants (we can bind to your AWS KMS). Role-based access, scoped service accounts, and mandatory 2FA for any staff with access to production stores.

6) Additional controls:
- Customer may opt for zero-retention mode for request payloads (no persistence) — this is gated behind an enterprise plan and a brief onboarding checklist.

I’ll paste these into the questionnaire in a clean format if you want. Marcos (cc) and Aditya are on thread for any infra-level clarifications.

Thanks,
Naomi
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Naomi —

This is very helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups from Legal: (A) Can you confirm that snapshots retained for 14 days are stored in the same region and encrypted with customer keys if we opt in? (B) For the 72-hour purge SLA, does that include removal from 3rd-party log sinks (we forward some webhook traces to a third-party SIEM at our side)?

Also, for the zero-retention option — can you outline any impacts on rate limiting / debugging support (we may need debug traces if we hit an outage).

Jordan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@sageworks.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — residency / retention + deletion SLA for hosted API

Jordan —

Quick technical clarifications from infra: (A) Yes, nightly snapshots are kept in the account's pinned region and can be encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (we support AWS KMS CMKs). You must request CMK binding during onboarding; we document the process in the workbook.

(B) The 72-hour purge SLA covers all data we control (primary storage, request-level logs, inference caches, and our backups). We do not have purging authority over copies of logs or webhooks that you have already forwarded to external systems (e.g., your SIEM). For completeness, our audit export will enumerate objects we purged and provide timestamps so you can correlate with any external retention. If you want, we can add a short statement for the questionnaire clarifying that external sinks must be purged by the recipient.

Zero-retention note: enabling zero-retention mode disables persistence of request payloads and outputs. This reduces post-incident debugging capability — in zero-retention we only retain aggregate telemetry and a minimal set of anonymized request metrics for 30 days. Rate limiting and SLA are unchanged, but debug-level troubleshooting (replaying inputs) is not possible. For customers who require on-call debugging, we recommend a time-limited capture window that can be enabled temporarily under a support agreement.

-Marcus
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@sageworks.ai>

Team —

Thanks for the clarity. Legal is happy with the wording and the 72-hour SLA paired with the 30-day GC on backups — they just want the questionnaire entry to be explicit that (1) SageWorks is responsible for purging any downstream copies it controls, and (2) Redwood will provide an audit export upon completion of a purge request.

If you can send a one-paragraph statement we can paste into the security questionnaire, we can close this out today. Also, please attach the residency matrix PDF and the workbook you mentioned.

Jordan
